title: 5b-2: component reconciliation + architectural events
description:
## Parent

sutra/44 (5b PRD: component discovery + vocabulary)

## What to build

Recompute path for component discovery. When Louvain runs again on a changed graph, reconcile new clusters against existing durable components using Jaccard overlap (>0.6 → match). Unmatched new clusters create new components. Unmatched existing components are marked dissolved. Detect and store architectural events: merge (two prior components collapsed into one cluster), split (one prior component spans two clusters), drift (>30% file shift between components). Events stored in `component_events` table (durable).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reconciliation matches new clusters to existing components via Jaccard overlap (threshold 0.6)
- [ ] Unmatched clusters create new components with auto-names
- [ ] Unmatched existing components marked dissolved with timestamp, hidden from normal queries
- [ ] Merge event emitted when two prior components map to one new cluster
- [ ] Split event emitted when one prior component's files span two new clusters
- [ ] Drift event emitted when >30% of a component's files shift to another component
- [ ] Events stored in component_events with type, involved component IDs, and timestamp
- [ ] Test: given prior components + new clustering → correct match/create/dissolve decisions
- [ ] Test: merge, split, drift detection with synthetic data

## Blocked by

- sutra/45 (5b-1: basic component discovery)

execution_record: 3 commits: schema+DB layer, core reconciliation+events+tests, orphan test rename. 367 tests pass (13 component tests: 7 existing + 6 new). Key decisions during implementation: (1) Jaccard threshold is >= 0.6 (inclusive), not > 0.6; (2) split/merge events also fire for dissolved components (not just matched); (3) tests use pinned resolution=1.0 to avoid auto_tune fragmentation on small cliques.

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex review (adversarial):

Verdict: needs-attention

1. [high] Merge detection treats any overlap as absorption — drift/split can produce false merge events. `detect_events` marks every cluster with files from 2+ prior components as a merge, then only excludes the component matched to *that same cluster*. A surviving component matched to a *different* cluster still appears in `absorbed[]`. In the drift test shape (A keeps 3 files, shifts 2 to B), this would emit a spurious merge on B absorbing A even though A is alive and matched elsewhere.

   Recommendation: Only include dissolved/unmatched components in `absorbed[]`. Add regression test that drift does not emit merge.

2. [medium] Split events omit resulting component IDs — detail only has file counts. `cluster_to_comp` is available but not used. This fails the AC requirement that events store involved component IDs. Makes split history hard to consume.

   Recommendation: Include target component IDs per cluster in split detail. Add test assertions.

messages.author: agent
messages.text: Fixed both codex review findings:\n1. Merge filter now uses `!matched_comps.contains(ci)` — only dissolved components appear in absorbed[]. Regression test confirms drift does not emit merge.\n2. Split detail now includes `targets` array with component_id + files per cluster. Test asserts presence."
